tagline.text: The Camotes' signature white-sand beach, stretching along the south of Pacijan Island

location.label: Location
location.text: Santiago Village (Santiago Bay), San Francisco, Pacijan Island, Camotes Islands, Cebu

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: March–May dry season (June–November is the rainy season; ferries vary with sea conditions)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half a day to 2 days and 1 night

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱2,500~4,500 (1 night, 2 days from Cebu, per person)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB), then a ferry

children.text: Santiago Beach is a broad stretch of white sand in Santiago village, San Francisco, on Pacijan Island in the Camotes Islands east of Cebu. The beach itself is free to enter, and it is known as the longest white-sand strip in the islands, a quiet place to swim and watch the sunset.

Santiago Beach lies on the south coast of Pacijan Island, one of the Camotes Islands that float in the Camotes Sea between mainland Cebu and Leyte. Administratively it belongs to Santiago village in the municipality of San Francisco, and travelers more often call it Santiago Bay or Santiago White Beach. San Francisco has 15 villages (barangays), and Santiago had a population of about
2,412 people
in the 2024 census. It is a small fishing village, so picture a low line of small resorts, eateries and cottages rather than big hotels towering behind the sand.

The beach's main features are its length and easy access. Local travel write-ups describe Santiago as the longest white-sand beach in the Camotes and a public beach anyone can enter without paying. Because it is maintained by the San Francisco local government, there is no entrance ticket booth, and you only pay when you rent a shaded cottage. The water is described as shallow and calm, easy for families with children. At low tide, however, the water draws far out, so there are better and worse times to swim; read the season guidance below as well.

Unlike Oslob or Moalboal on mainland Cebu, tour buses do not flood in here, and many reviews say you may have the beach almost to yourself on weekdays. On weekends and holidays, though, families crossing from Cebu and local groups renting videoke machines can make it noisy. If you want quiet, aim for weekday mornings; if you want the mood at dusk, walk to one end of the beach.

Santiago Beach is less a sight that fills a whole day than a home base for a Camotes trip. The most common pattern is to stay in front of the beach, ride a motorbike during the day to Lake Danao, the caves and the cliff-diving resorts, then return to this stretch of sand at dusk for dinner. This guide lays out, in order, what a traveler coming from Korea via Cebu needs for one to two days here.

blocks.title: The longest white-sand beach in the islands

children.text: The shoreline is long and the sand fine enough that you can walk from one end of the beach to the other. Local guides call it the longest white-sand beach in the Camotes. The feel changes from section to section as you walk, so take your time.

blocks.title: A public beach with no entrance fee

children.text: The beach is a public one maintained by the San Francisco local government, so there is no fee to enter the beach itself. You pay only when you rent a shaded cottage, and you can swim here even if you are not a resort guest. Rules may differ in the area in front of a resort, so check on the spot.

The water is clear and shallow, so unless the waves are high it is easy to wade in and swim. Some sections are described as shallow enough for children to play in. One review says the rocky area on the right side (facing the sea) is good for swimming, and that it is mostly low tide there, so around 10 AM is recommended.

Many reviews praise the sunset from one end of the beach, and at night the stars are said to be easy to see over a fishing village with little light. Eating dinner at a beachfront restaurant while watching the sunset is the most typical thing to do here.

Volleyball, kayaking and rides on a motorized banca (a small outrigger boat) are said to be available for a low fee. Some people camp in tents, but you must ask permission first. Prices change from year to year, so ask directly and agree on the price.

Small eateries and shops that rent videoke machines cluster around the beach. Pito's Sutokil, known for the Cebuano seafood dish sutokil, is described as reasonably priced; the wait is long, but reviewers say the food is worth it.

blocks.title: A base for touring the Camotes

children.text: Santiago Beach is within motorbike range of Consuelo port, and it pairs well in a day with the Camotes' best-known sights such as Lake Danao, Timubo Cave, Mangodlong Rock and Buho Rock. An efficient plan is to relax at the beach, tour the island by day and come back in the evening.

items.title: One night from Cebu
items.subtitle: Beach rest and an island loop

children.text: Take a bus or van from the Cebu City north bus terminal to Danao. It takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
and costs about
. If you take OceanJet instead, use the boat from Pier 1 (Cebu City) to Poro port.
Take the Jomalia ferry from Danao port to Consuelo port, about
2 hours
. Sailing times vary by day and season, so check with the operator the day before.
From Consuelo port, ride a motorbike or habal-habal (motorbike taxi) to Santiago Beach, about
8.6 km
from the port. Drop your bags at your lodging and have lunch at a beachfront restaurant.
Walk along the beach and swim. Play in the water in the shallow stretches.
Watch the sunset from one end of the beach and have sutokil or grilled seafood for dinner at a beachfront restaurant.
Rent a motorbike and visit one or two of Lake Danao, Timubo Cave, Mangodlong Rock and Buho Rock, then return to Consuelo port in time for an afternoon boat.
The last boat's time changes with the day and the weather, and some sailings are cancelled. On your return day, plan so that you arrive at the port with time to spare.

items.title: Half-day plan
items.subtitle: If you are already staying on the island

children.text: Have breakfast at your lodging and stroll the beach in the quiet morning.
If it is low tide, swim and snorkel in the rocky area on the right side of the beach. It is better to bring your own snorkeling gear.
Have lunch at a beachfront restaurant and rest in a cottage.
Try a kayak or banca for a low fee, and come back before sunset.
Flights run frequently from Manila (NAIA) to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB), about
1 hour 20 minutes
in the air.
From Cebu airport, go to Pier 1 in Cebu City (OceanJet) or to Danao port (Jomalia) to board a boat.
There are also sea routes from Manila to Cebu, but they take long and their operation changes, so flying is the practical choice.

The Jomalia fast craft that ran from Mactan to Consuelo is reported to have stopped sailing recently, so confirm before you plan on it.
Boat schedules and fares change often, and sailings may be cancelled in bad weather. Check the operator's official announcements, such as its Facebook page, for the situation on the day.
Santiago Beach is about
8.6 km
from Consuelo port and can be reached by motorbike, habal-habal, tricycle or van. A short habal-habal ride is reported at about

Motorbike rental is about
a day plus fuel, and a multicab with a driver is about
a day depending on vehicle size.

Santiago Beach is a place for playing in the sea, so weather and waves affect it directly. Local guides generally pick the dry season, March to May, as the most reliable time. Skies are clear and the sea calm then, so beach activities and boats are both steady. Midday in April and May is very hot, so bring a hat and sunscreen.

June to November is the rainy season, with frequent showers, and boats between Cebu and the Camotes may be cancelled or delayed depending on sea conditions. When a typhoon crosses the Philippines, it is safer to postpone your trip. Within a day, one review says around 10 AM is a good time to swim in the rocky area on the right of the beach because of the low tide and the light, and the sunset is best from one end of the beach at dusk.

Right on the beach there are small resorts such as Santiago Bay Garden & Resort, with standard rooms reported at roughly ₱1,000~3,000 (villas and family rooms cost more; there is no confirmed official rate card, so ask before booking). Camotes Backpackers Hostel in the same village is listed with air-conditioned double rooms from about ₱995. On the coast near Consuelo port are Mangodlong Rock Resort and Mangodlong Paradise Beach Resort, whose cliffside pool and views are well known on the island. Rooms fill quickly in peak season and on weekends, so book ahead.

Meals are taken at the small eateries around the beach. Grilled fish, sutokil (a Cebuano dish that combines a raw fish preparation with grilled meat) and rice meals are the staples, and prices are said to be slightly lower than in central Cebu. Some shops rent videoke machines and stay open late, so if you want a quiet night, check where your lodging is. Many shops on the island do not take cards and ATMs may be scarce, so bring plenty of cash.
There is no entrance fee for the beach, so if someone asks for money there, first ask what it is for.
Boat times are the biggest variable. Reconfirm your return boat time with your lodging, and arrive at the port at least
1 hour
before departure.
One review says the rocky area on the right of the beach is good for swimming around 10 AM at low tide, so check the tide before you go.
Many stretches have little shade. Bring a wide-brimmed hat, sunscreen and plenty of drinking water.
It is best to bring your own snorkeling gear. Whether rentals are available locally is uncertain.
When you rent a motorbike, check the helmet, your license and the fuel level.
There is almost no lighting on the beach after sunset. Bring a small flashlight or use your phone light.
Carry plenty of cash and small change (₱20 and ₱50 notes) to make paying for habal-habal rides and cottages easy.
Boats to the Camotes are often cancelled or delayed by weather, so plan with slack so that your return does not collide with a flight or other commitments.
At low tide, when the water draws far out, some stretches are poor for swimming. Check the tide.
Beachfront eateries and videoke can be noisy late into the night, so choose your lodging with that in mind.
Wear sandals or aqua shoes when entering rocky areas.
Do not leave your belongings unattended; keep them in the cottage or your lodging.
Camp only in places where you have been given permission, and carry your trash out.
